## Page 1 | H5-A: cutoff study extract

**GreenWaste is a fictional training case.** This supplied extract and page 2's figures are your source; there is no separate report to find.

### §1 | Who and what determined participation?

GreenWaste offers equipment subsidies, installation help and training. The city file has **10,000 businesses**: 4,794 participants and 5,206 others. Businesses with efficiency scores **58 or below participated**; those above 58 did not. Higher scores mean more efficient. The running variable is the score; **58 is the cutoff**. This rule is followed in the file, but it is not a lottery.

### §2 | What does the fitted result compare?

The local model uses **545 businesses within two points of 58 (scores 56-60)**. The outcome is annual waste cost in AED per business, measured **12 months after**. Separate straight cost/score slopes are fitted on either side. The coefficient compares the fitted costs approaching 58 from the participating side versus the non-participating side. It is not the average gap across the whole city, or the small raw mean gap on a card.

```{r, results='asis'}
html_out(d5_table())
```

### §3 | Which checks are supplied or missing?

A five-point window (scores 53-63) uses **1,260 businesses** and estimates **-784 AED**, interval **-934 to -634**. This sensitivity comparison does not prove causal validity. **Pre-programme manager age also jumps at 58: about -5.3 years in the five-point window.** It raises a concern about who is compared and other explanations for a cost jump. It does not prove a particular bias. No score-setting or manipulation diagnostic is supplied. The evaluator should investigate the scoring process, who could influence scores and other discontinuities. A causal reading requires comparable businesses immediately either side apart from programme access, without relevant sorting or other important jumps.

### §4 | What follows for the decision?

On a positive-reduction scale, the local estimate is **721 AED**, interval **498-943**. Both are below the fictional **1,000 AED annual-saving minimum**, conditional on the model. Precision does not resolve the design concern. Most city participants are outside this local window. A result at the cutoff is not an estimated average effect for typical participants or the whole city. Full programme costs and national effects are not supplied.

<div class="source-note">Source: corrected evaluation_data_GreenWaste_simple.csv, city records; calculations in day2_session2_review.R and shared case model. HC2 robust intervals. Figures are actual records and fitted lines except the explicitly hypothetical sorting illustration.</div>

</div>

## Page 2 | H5-A: visual reference

### The fitted jump at 58: two-point window

```{r, results='asis'}
html_out(d5_plot(2,TRUE))
```

Dots are actual city businesses with scores 53-63. Shading marks scores 56-60 used in the main model. Lines approach the cutoff; the red gap is between their fitted limits.

```{r, results='asis'}
html_out(d5_windows())
```

### A pre-programme characteristic: manager age

<div class="age-figure">
```{r, results='asis'}
html_out(d5_plot(5,TRUE,TRUE))
```
</div>

This age discontinuity is a credibility concern, not a GreenWaste effect on age. Optional extension: adding age to the two-point model gives **-632 AED**, HC2 interval **-857 to -407**. Adjustment alone does not establish a valid local comparison.

</div>

## Page 3 | Q1-Q2: arithmetic and interpretation

### Q1 | Record your group's raw card gap

Card letter: ______. Use your **separate A-H card**, six businesses per side. Costs are rounded to ten AED. Scores are displayed to one decimal, but groups follow the unrounded score.

| Calculation | At/below 58 | Above 58 |
|---|---|---|
| Sum of six costs | __________ | __________ |
| Mean: sum divided by 6 | __________ | __________ |

At/below mean minus above mean: __________________ AED.

Place the letter and gap in the **raw-gap lane** on the number line. Why might other groups get different gaps?

### Q2 | Read the fitted local jump

<div class="writing tall"></div>

Interpret the coefficient: comparison, sign, units, timing and local population. Name what must be credible before calling it an effect.

<div class="writing tall"></div>
